clinician.trajectory_summary: A 65-year-old man with diabetes and hypertension presented in late October 2020 with acute-onset dysphagia for solids and liquids, nasal intonation of speech, mild bifacial weakness, decreased bilateral palatal movements, and poor pharyngeal reflex. He had recovered from mild COVID-19 infection in September 2020 (treated with remdesivir, RT-PCR negative by late September). Diagnostic workup confirmed seropositive myasthenia gravis: serum anti-AChR antibodies elevated at 4.5 nmol/L (normal <0.40), repetitive nerve stimulation showed significant decremental response (nasalis 41%, trapezius 18.1%), anti-MuSK antibodies negative, and intravenous neostigmine produced marked improvement in swallowing. Imaging studies (MRI brain/spinal cord, high-resolution CT thorax) ruled out structural causes and thymoma. On day 8 of admission, the patient developed neck and respiratory muscle weakness (single breath count 8, MGC 17) with type II respiratory failure (PCo2 52 mm Hg), meeting criteria for myasthenic crisis. He was intubated and connected to mechanical ventilation.

final.trajectory_summary: A 65-year-old man with diabetes and hypertension presented in late October 2020 with acute-onset dysphagia for solids and liquids, nasal intonation of speech, mild bifacial weakness, decreased bilateral palatal movements, and poor pharyngeal reflex. He had recovered from mild COVID-19 infection in September 2020 (treated with remdesivir, RT-PCR negative by late September). Diagnostic workup confirmed seropositive myasthenia gravis: serum anti-AChR antibodies elevated at 4.5 nmol/L (normal <0.40), repetitive nerve stimulation showed significant decremental response (nasalis 41%, trapezius 18.1%), anti-MuSK antibodies negative, and intravenous neostigmine produced marked improvement in swallowing. Imaging studies (MRI brain/spinal cord, high-resolution CT thorax) ruled out structural causes and thymoma. On day 8 of admission, the patient developed neck and respiratory muscle weakness (single breath count 8, MGC 17) with type II respiratory failure (PCo2 52 mm Hg), meeting criteria for myasthenic crisis. He was intubated and connected to mechanical ventilation.
